answer: Join budgets per network neighbourhood: each ASN or /24 block gets a small quota of new identities per epoch that refills slowly, and joins past it wait in a public queue. One operator's garden of sybils can then grow only as fast as its scarcest input, distinct clean networks. Residential proxies cost real money per address per month, so near the zenith of a farm the rent outruns the rewards. Honest newcomers on a crowded campus network can be vouched out of the queue by one established member, so the network stays an oasis for them.
